nodes.label: Carrom module (own points-race grammar)
nodes.rationale: Not a boardgame or set-based preset — carrom is a points race, so it gets its own module with ICF as the system preset and everything configurable.

nodes.label: Board -> Game -> Match structure
nodes.rationale: ICF Law 56a: a game is 25 points or eight boards; Law 57: matches are best of three. A tie after the eighth board plays an extra board (Law 56b), with a 'draw' house-rule switch for leagues that want drawn matches.

nodes.label: Queen cap checked against pre-board score
nodes.rationale: Laws 52(b)(i) and 54 credit the queen up to and including 21 and remove it at 22, so the bonus is evaluated against the pre-board score — a board's own coin points can never lift the winner past the cap for that same board.

nodes.label: queenFollowsBoard house-rule switch
nodes.rationale: Laws 53b/53c mean a loser-covered queen scores for nobody under ICF — the earlier draft's guess that she transfers to the board winner was wrong, so the transfer became an explicit opt-in switch defaulting to false.

nodes.label: carrom.board.summary event
nodes.rationale: Strike-by-strike is umpire-grade and impractical courtside, so the board result is the natural default unit of fidelity.

nodes.label: carrom.toss as pre-start sport event (PROMPT-16 deviation)
nodes.rationale: The prompt asked for a core.start {firstBreak} payload, but core event payloads are kernel-owned strict-empty objects per spec 03 §2, so the toss became a pre-start sport event following the cricket.toss precedent.

nodes.label: Break alternation tracking
nodes.rationale: Law 49a: the toss winner breaks board 1 and the turn passes alternately; Law 56b's fresh toss before an extra board is deliberately not modelled — alternation simply continues.

nodes.label: Carrom cascade with board_ratio key
nodes.rationale: Games ride the shared sets_won/sets_lost comparator keys (the badminton precedent) and board points ride points_won/lost; no federation cascade is universal, so ours is documented as house-standard and overridable.
